edge.title: Late capped RRE extrapolation of hidden weights every 5 steps
edge.summary: Adds a late reduced-rank-extrapolation (RRE) overlay to the unchanged #30 optimizer: from step 2820 the flattened vector of all Muon hidden matrices is snapshotted after every step, and every 5 steps (2825, 2830, …, 2925: 21 times) an RRE combination of the last 4 snapshots (3 consecutive step differences, ridge 1e-6) is computed, damped 0.875 toward the current weights, capped at 0.1% of the global hidden-weight norm and written back, keeping momentum and SOAP state. Training stops at 2925 (RUN_STOP_STEP) while the 3020/3050 schedule horizon stays as in #30. Because of how the RRE weights are accumulated (see caveats), in practice each jump is a capped pull back along the last few steps, closer to iterate averaging than to forward extrapolation.

changes.label: Late RRE overlay on hidden matrices
changes.detail: Muon.step calls _maybe_extrapolate after the all_gather: from next_step ≥ 2820 it appends the flattened Muon params to a 4-deep history and every 5th step (through EXTRAPOLATION_STOP_STEP=2925) runs rre_extrapolate with damping 0.875 and a 1e-3 relative cap, writes the result back and restarts the history; momentum is kept (EXTRAPOLATION_RESET_MOMENTUM=0).

changes.label: Training loop ends at 2925
changes.detail: run_stop_step (env RUN_STOP_STEP=2925) ends the loop with a final validation; train_steps=3020 still defines the μ cooldown (2920–3020) and PowerCool end stays 3050.

changes.label: Env-driven experiment harness
changes.detail: Alternative extrapolators (MPE, MPE-Sidi, Anderson, VEA, STEA, quadratic, RRE blends/tsvd/subspace, layer/tensor-wise RRE), taper/block caps, momentum projection, LR sprint, checkpoint save/load and model/batch env knobs are added but inactive in the record config.

edge.parent_check: consistent: behaviorally identical to #30 apart from the RRE hook and the 2925 stop; the extracted script defaults EXTRAPOLATION_NAME='none', and the RRE settings come from env vars printed in all 8 seed logs (identical to the README and train_gpt_simple_rre_pr300_2925.py)
edge.noise: ~700 lines of inactive extrapolation variants and harness knobs (taper/block caps, momentum projection, LR sprint, checkpointing, MODEL_*/batch env overrides at their defaults), SEED readable from env, extra extrap_* fields in log lines.

mechanisms.name: Late capped RRE extrapolation
mechanisms.explain: From next_step 2820 the concatenated Muon weights are pushed into a history of at most 4 snapshots; when next_step % 5 == 0 and the history is full, rre_extrapolate forms the 3 differences U, solves (UUᵀ + 1e-6·tr/3·I)c = 1, normalizes Σc = 1, and returns x_last − Σ_j γ_j Δ_j with γ = reverse-cumsum(c). The result is lerped 0.875 of the way from the current weights, the global move is capped at 1e-3·‖θ‖, written back into every hidden matrix, and the history restarts from the new point (so each jump uses the last 3 optimizer steps); momentum and SOAP statistics are left untouched.

caveats: In the script captured in the logs every RRE knob is an env var with an off default (EXTRAPOLATION_NAME='none', EVERY=20, DAMPING=1.0, MAX_REL=0, RESET_MOMENTUM=1); the record values come from the run environment, as printed in every log header (rre every=5 start=2820 checkpoints=4 damping=0.875 max_rel=0.001 reset_momentum=False stop=2925, run_stop_step=2925). Code detail: γ is the reverse cumulative sum of c, so the output equals x₀ + c₀Δ₁ + (c₀+c₁)Δ₂ (x₀ = oldest snapshot) rather than textbook RRE/RNA Σcᵢxᵢ; with c ≥ 0 (typical for noisy late steps) the damped, capped correction pulls the weights back along the last steps, i.e. capped iterate averaging rather than forward extrapolation. Logs agree: extrap_rel is pinned at the 1e-3 cap through step 2870 in all 8 seeds, then falls in exact proportion to the LR (≈6.7e-4 at 2925 in every seed, ≈1.6× the per-step relative move lr·0.3825), i.e. a near-deterministic ~1.6-step move. README's 'k=4' counts stored iterates (3 difference vectors). Table notes p=0.168 vs #30; runs used world_size=1 (single H100).
